Zuma Endgame
17 February 2018

Sound Up Jacob Zuma
No life should be lost in my name. And also, the ANC should never be divided in my name. I have therefore come to the decision to resign as president of the Republic with immediate effect.

Voice
The final curtain call for a president who to so many had overstayed his welcome. After years of pleading for his resignation, which climaxed in 2017 with mass mobilisations by civil society, opposition parties and the general public, President Jacob Zuma finally put the country out of it’s misery on Valentine’s day this week.

Link Devi
But Jacob Zuma kept everyone wondering right until the bitter end. It all began last sunday when deputy president Cyril Ramaphosa, speaking in Cape Town, told supporters we know you want closure on this matter.

Voice
Pressure had been mounting on the ANC to make a call on who would lead the country after the State of the Nation address had been delayed the previous week, an unheard of event.

Link Devi
After supporting their president through every conceivable scandal over the past 9 years, the ANC finally relented on Tuesday. Secretary General, and long time Zuma ally, Ace Magashule, told journalists the ANC had decided to recall Zuma.

Sound Up Ace Magashule
In its wisdom the NEC decided as follows, one: To recall its deployee comrade Jacob Zuma in accordance with rule 12.2.21.2 of the ANC constitution.

Voice
The decision effectively sealed President Zuma’s fate. But rumours were rife that the president wasn’t about to go anywhere. Political analyst Moeletsi Mbeki says he had his doubts about Zuma towing the party line.

Sound Up Moeletsi Mbeki
I was a little bit surprised I must say because I thought Jacob Zuma had a lot more guts… I remember Mandela once telling a famous president, I think of the United States to jump into the lake. I thought Zuma was going to tell the National Executive Committee to do it’s damndest and institute it’s vote of no confidence.

Voice
But pressure on the president was mounting from all sides. In the early hours of wednesday morning his friends, the Gupta’s, had their Saxonwold mansion raided. The president’s son Duduzane house was also searched but he wasn’t home. Several arrests were made in connection with the controversial Estina Dairy Farm project in the Free State. Former ANC MP Makhozi Khoza, who resigned from the party last year and received death threats after strongly criticising Jacob Zuma, welcomed the move.

Sound Up Makhosi Khoza
I’m an African and I love Africa. If there is one thing that South Africa must do, it’s to get those shiny suits being replaced with those orange overalls in prison. I would love to see them going to jail. Because if we don’t act now, we are setting a wrong precedent for our young democracy.

Voice
Wednesday saw an extraordinary meeting take place in parliament, where the Chief Whips of the main opposition parties and the ANC all agreed to band together in a motion of no confidence in Zuma if he refused to resign. Moeletsi Mbeki doubts we’ll see more of that kind of cooperation in the future.

Sound Up Moeletsi Mbeki
This is what’s called an elite pact. It’s the elite making itself feel good, we’ve got a fall guy. So we don’t have to examine what the ANC was doing. We don’t have to examine what the opposition parties are doing. We just blame this one man so they were all great buddies there.

Devi Link
On wednesday the drama continued as a defiant Zuma appeared in an impromptu SABC interview to tell us his side of the story. Incredibly, he was asking what had he done wrong?

Sound Up President Jacob Zuma
We have got a lot of resolutions to be dealing with, we are spending more time discussing Zuma must go. I don’t understand why?

Voice
The president may have forgotten the constitutional court’s scathing judgment against him on the Nkandla debacle or the 783 charges of fraud, money laundering and racketeering he still faces. Moeletsi Mbeki says Zuma has been made the fall guy for the ANC.

Sound Up Moeletsi Mbeki
Mbeki: You see the removal of Jacob Zuma is a cover up for the whole ANC leadership collaboration with corruption in South Africa. Zuma is a sacrificial lamb that the ANC is making. The corruption, and the wave of corruption that we’re seeing today, was permitted by the ANC.

Voice
The president also made some other outlandish claims during the interview, one being that he had not supported the recall of Thabo Mbeki that led to Zuma becoming president.

Sound Up Jacob Zuma
When the NEC discussed this matter, I was one of those who were in fact saying we should not recall comrade president Mbeki, because you will be creating a bad precedent.

Voice
According to former general Siphiwe Nyanda, an ex Zuma cabinet minister and former head of the SANDF, Jacob Zuma did support the recall of Thabo Mbeki.

Sound Up Siphiwe
Siphiwe: I really don’t recall Zuma standing behind those people who were calling for caution on the action against Thabo Mbeki.

Devi: We would have remembered that if that happened?

Siphiwe: Definitely.

Voice
Nyanda was one of the MK veterans who in 2016 sent a memorandum to the ANC, complaining that the removal of then finance minister Nhlanhla Nene sent a message that all was not well within the state.

Devi: Sometimes people should listen to their elders?

Siphiwe: Yes. If the ANC had listened to our

Voice
Finally, late on wednesday night, Zuma caved under the pressure.

Sound Up Jacob Zuma
I have therefore come to the decision to resign as president of the Republic with immediate effect.

Voice
Eight people appeared in the Bloemfontein Magistrates court on thursday,amongst them Varun Gupta and former Oakbay CEO Nazeem Howa. The suspects were released on bail of between R10 000 and R200 000 each. The Hawks have confirmed that Ajay Gupta is now a fugitive from justice and reports suggest that Duduzane Zuma might appear in the dock soon.

Devi:
Thursday saw what many are calling the dawn of a new era in South African Politics. With none of the opposition parties putting forward their own candidates, Cyril Ramaphosa became the fifth democratically elected president of the Republic.

Sound Up Chief Justice Mogoeng Mogoeng
I declare the honourable Matamela Cyril Ramaphosa duly elected president of the Republic of South Africa.

Voice
One of the greatest challenges for the new President will be kickstarting a floundering economy and creating jobs for the millions of unemployed around the country. Goolam Ballim is the chief economist and Global Head of Research at Standard Bank. He says we should not underestimate the damage done to our economy over the past decade.

Sound Up Goolam Ballim
Devi: Would it be fair to say that under Jacob Zuma’s reign, the South African economy has suffered setbacks?

Goolam: The cost of the Zuma presidency has been enormous. We estimate for example that over the last decade, the South African economy has foregone about R1 trillion in GDP. Put differently, if we were able to maintain the performance that South Africa mustered in the mid 2000’s, the economy would have been 25% bigger.

Sound Up Nyanda
The African National Congress needs to put it’s house in order so that the country grows it’s economy, and South Africans over a period of time improve there livelihoods.

Voice
Makhosi Khoza says despite the jubilation after the disastrous Zuma years, President Ramaphosa has a long way to go before she’ll be convinced he is able to turn the ANC around.

Sound Up Makhosi Khoza
As a child that grew up in the ANC, to me I saw the ANC really losing it. Even those great statesmen that we are accepting today, they were not there to come out and actually say this is wrong. They were happy to play along for a long as their turn comes.

Voice
Globally President Cyril Ramaphosa’s appointment has been greeted with goodwill and the Rand soared on two and a half year high’s this week. But only time will tell whether he will surpass the incredibly low bar set by his predecessor.

Sound Up Makhosi Khoza
Devi: What do you think Jacob Zuma’s legacy is?

Makhosi: Institutionalisation of corruption, undoing all the gains that women made since 1994. And I really do think that’s he’s left behind a lot of victims, because corruption is not a victimless crime. The fact that we have such a high rate of unemployment in this country, the fact that investors have lost so much confidence in South Africa, that is Zuma’s legacy and I’m glad he’s gone.
